notes: SHIP v1.14.396 - THE RACK WAS NEVER REFUSED A CONTEXT. THE CHECK WAS ASKING THE WRONG QUESTION. Root cause of the blank rack, found with the M0 instrument on the first run and proven in-browser. three.js r128 creates a WebGL2RenderingContext. Per spec, a canvas that already holds a webgl2 context returns NULL for getContext('webgl') and for getContext('experimental-webgl') - a mismatched type is refused, not created. Every site that verified the renderer by asking for 'webgl' therefore got null from a PERFECTLY LIVE context and concluded REFUSED. In bw_mount3D that conclusion is load-bearing: it calls say(), which does mount.innerHTML = '' and DESTROYS THE WORKING RENDERER, replacing it with the error card. The diagnostic was causing the failure it reported. EVIDENCE (desktop Chrome, live v1.14.395, real deployment, rack c1:001): the app showed 'webgl context REFUSED' with rackCtx=REFUSED and rackOwner=bw-mount - while, at that same moment, the browser granted 20 fresh WebGL contexts back to back and a new THREE.WebGLRenderer constructed cleanly with isContextLost false. So context pressure was never the cause. Direct proof: THREE.WebGLRenderer -> getContext().constructor.name === 'WebGL2RenderingContext', and that same canvas answers getContext('webgl') false, getContext('webgl2') true. Isolated proof: a canvas given webgl2 returns null for 'webgl' and 'experimental-webgl' forever after. THIS EXPLAINS THE WHOLE ARC. .390's twelve re-arms each built a working renderer and the same wrong check killed it twelve times. .394 removing the re-arm did not help because the re-arm was never the problem. The device reporting 'WebGL support: true' alongside 'context REFUSED' was not a contradiction: the capability probe used a FRESH canvas, which grants webgl1 happily, while the rack canvas held webgl2. And Command surrendering its renderer in .394 was addressing contention that did not exist. THE FIX. One helper, phantom_readGL(cv), tries webgl2 then webgl then experimental-webgl, and every read-back of an existing canvas's context now routes through it - so the bug cannot recur at a fourth site. Three call sites corrected: the load-bearing check in bw_mount3D, diag()'s rackCtx line, and PhantomGL's observer read-back. TWO OF THOSE THREE WERE SHIPPED IN M0 EARLIER TODAY WITH THE IDENTICAL FLAW - the observer was reporting 1 refused for a live context, which is exactly the blind spot the instrument existed to eliminate, and it is corrected here. phantom_webglCapable is deliberately NOT changed: it probes a BARE canvas for device capability, where webgl1 is the correct floor. Note that phantom_readGL is only ever called on canvases already known to hold a context, because asking a bare canvas CREATES one. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PROGRAM. The blueprint named F3 - iOS asynchronous GPU reclaim after forceContextLoss - as the root cause. That was wrong, and it is corrected in the record. F3 remains a real latent hazard and the I6 reclaim barrier is still worth building, but it is prevention, not the repair. M2 must be re-scoped against evidence rather than against the old theory. SCENE UNTOUCHED. Materials, the section A light rig, fog, tone mapping, tray geometry, type colours, bezel strips, floor, reflection and boot are all exactly as they were; this ship changes only which question is asked about an existing context. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, CSS braces 4557/4557, line endings preserved, three-stamp lockstep. DEVICE-VERIFY: cold load with the service worker cleared, open Build, and the rack should DRAW. If it does, the eight-ship arc from .389 closes here.
